design: Targeted discount (RF, simplified): a flat £175 to GB households on means-tested benefits or whose highest individual income is under £24,000
note: Simplified fixed-payment illustration of the Resolution Foundation's unit-rate discount. Counted as HBAI income by assumption, by analogy with DWP's treatment of the Warm Home Discount.
assumptions: A flat £175 per eligible household, not RF's discount on gas and electricity unit rates (£175 is RF's average per eligible household).
The income test uses annual income, not the previous three months' income.
Full take-up: every eligible household receives it, including those that would have to self-declare.

design: Warm Home Discount top-up: an extra £100 to households that receive the rebate under the scheme's rules (England and Wales qualifying benefits, Scotland's core group), paid from taxation

sensitivities.label: Receipt rates (85% Pension Credit, 70% other), expected value
Other-benefits receipt rate 60% (impact assessment sensitivity), expected value
Other-benefits receipt rate 80% (impact assessment sensitivity), expected value
England and Wales only (no Scottish top-up)
Scotland: every household on a qualifying benefit, as if the broader group were paid like the core group
Caseload set to DESNZ's estimate of about 6m recipient households

note: Eligible (7.3m households): in England and Wales, households where anyone receives Pension Credit, Universal Credit, Housing Benefit, income-related ESA (the scheme year's eligibility statement); in Scotland, the core group that receives the rebate without applying. Not every eligible household receives the rebate: the claimant or partner must be named on a participating supplier's electricity account and matched to DWP records. DESNZ's receipt rates are applied by policyengine-uk's seeded draw per household: 85% of households with Pension Credit and 70% of other eligible households (5.2m recipients, against about 6m in DESNZ's estimate for winter 2025/26).

design: £300 Cost of Living Payment to households on means-tested benefits
Cap freeze: electricity and gas unit rates and standing charges held at April–June 2026 levels (£1,641 typical bill)
note: Price restoration, not a payment: each household's forecast bill minus its bill at April–June 2026 tariffs for the same kWh (seasonal profile), floored at zero. Outside HBAI income, so no poverty effect. UK-wide, with Northern Ireland on GB prices as a proxy.

design: Keep 0% VAT on domestic electricity from July 2027 to March 2028, beyond the Budget's extension to June 2027 (UK-wide)
note: Additional relief only: the Budget's zero rate to 30 June 2027 is already in the baseline. Price cut, costed from bills; not in HBAI income, so no poverty effect.

design: Move remaining levies to taxation: £120 off a typical electricity bill, as a share of each GB electricity bill
note: Price cut, costed from bills; not in HBAI income, so no poverty effect.
